## Statement

Eligibility and comparator decisions taken while assembling the evidence base can materially change an indirect comparison by changing which studies, populations and contrasts are represented, and this is demonstrated rather than hypothetical: a multiverse of 9216 indirect comparison meta-analyses of nalmefene versus naltrexone reported a Janus effect (Palpacuer et al. 2019, doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3), and a multiverse over all possible antidepressant networks found 172 of 231 pairwise comparisons showing opposite effects between the 1st and 99th percentiles (Vinatier et al. 2024, doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848). What remains open is that multiverse reporting is not required or routinely performed in sponsor submissions, and there is no accepted criterion for which alternative networks count as defensible. Selection changes how relevant the assembled evidence is to an externally defined target population; it does not by itself define the target estimand.

## Why it is open

The evidence set is assembled by the party that reports the result, and every downstream analysis conditions on the assembled network, so no covariate adjustment recovers the comparisons that were excluded. The tools to expose this now exist and their published applications show inclusion choices can flip the direction of an estimate, but nothing obliges a sponsor submission to report one, and the demonstrations to date sit in the general synthesis literature rather than in HTA practice. An undefined multiverse over all defensible networks also reintroduces analyst discretion and multiplicity, so the missing piece is a transparent rule for what counts as defensible rather than the technique itself.

## What has been tried

::: {.table-scroll}

| Work | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [Vinatier et al. 2024, BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848) | Multiverse analysis covering all possible network meta-analyses over treatment combinations across 522 antidepressant trials and 116,477 patients, quantifying how far conclusions move with the assembly step. |
| [Palpacuer et al. 2019, BMC Medicine](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3) | Enumerates 9216 indirect comparison meta-analyses of nalmefene versus naltrexone by varying eligibility criteria and analytic model, showing that inclusion decisions alone can reverse the direction of the comparison. |
| [Guelimi et al. 2025, BMC Medical Research Methodology](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12874-025-02558-6) | Quantifies how inclusion criteria and other methodological choices change network meta-analysis conclusions in psoriasis; shows sensitivity over alternative networks is operational. |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

The multiverse machinery exists and the work is to require and discipline it rather than to invent it: specify transparent rules for which alternative evidence sets are defensible, then report the estimate across them as a matter of course. Protocol-first feasibility assessment that fixes eligibility before results are known addresses the outcome-aware part of the problem that a multiverse cannot, since a multiverse run after the fact still starts from a chosen frame. Applying target-trial emulation to the construction of the evidence set rather than to a single analysis remains unevidenced; the literature auditor could not verify any published instance and Grok also left it open.

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Multiverse analysis over the assembled evidence set has been demonstrated for indirect comparisons and for network meta-analysis and shows that inclusion decisions can flip the direction of the estimate; what remains open is that it is not routinely required or performed in sponsor submissions, and there is no accepted criterion for which alternative networks count as defensible.

**The source said.** "Eligibility and comparator decisions taken while assembling the evidence base can induce a favorable network or a favorable target population before any modeling begins, and only one of the defensible networks is ever shown."

**What was wrong with it.** The source presented multiverse analysis over defensible networks as an emerging direction and said alternative networks are never reported; the literature auditor found two published multiverses of exactly that object (Palpacuer et al. 2019, doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3; Vinatier et al. 2024, doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848), with a third for inclusion criteria in psoriasis (Guelimi et al. 2025, doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02558-6). GPT-5.6 Sol separately rejected the conflation of the population represented by the selected studies with an externally defined target population, and struck the universal claims that every inclusion decision is outcome-aware and that alternatives are never shown.

**Dissent.** grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): The claim that eligibility and comparator choices can favor a network or target population before modeling, and that only one defensible network is typically shown, remains faithful for HTA/ITC practice. Recent work does, however, implement the multiverse response for treatment/network assembly in evidence synthesis, so the problem is not open as if no method existed. Vinatier et al. (2024) ran a multiverse covering all possible NMAs on different treatment combinations in antidepressants and showed large vibration of effects, especially for indirect comparisons. Guelimi et al. (2025) quantified how inclusion criteria and other methodological choices change NMA conclusions in psoriasis and explicitly contrasted their design with prior all-possible-networks work. These papers substantiate C1/C4 as live, demonstrated issues and give a usable multiverse template. They do not solve sponsor-side selective assembly, protocol-first eligibility fixed before knowing results, or target-trial emulation applied to the evidence set itself (C3); those remain open. RoB-NMA (2025) and PRISMA-NMA update work improve transparency of synthesis bias but do not replace multiverse reporting of defensible networks.

Literature and prior-art check
:   **partially-solved / overstated.** I retrieved two published multiverse analyses of exactly the object this entry proposes as future work, both in indirect comparison settings. Palpacuer 2019 BMC Medicine enumerated 9216 indirect comparison meta-analyses of nalmefene vs naltrexone by varying eligibility (condition, abstinence, sex, comorbidity, psychological support, dose, duration, outcome, publication status, risk of bias) and analytic model, and reported a 'Janus effect'. Vinatier 2024 BMJ EBM ran the multiverse over network composition itself: all possible NMAs over treatment combinations across 522 antidepressant trials and 116,477 patients. Claim 1 and claim 2 are therefore not merely plausible but empirically demonstrated. Claim 4, however, is written as if multiverse analysis over defensible networks were a promising future direction ('Emerging' maturity); it has been executed at scale and published in general medical journals. The why_open sentence 'Defensible alternative networks usually exist and are never reported' is contradicted by these two papers. Claim 3 (target-trial emulation applied to evidence-set construction) I could not verify; the only candidate I found was in an obscure venue I will not cite.
    Cites doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848: Executes the entry's proposed direction: a multiverse over all defensible network compositions, quantifying how far conclusions move with the assembly step..
    Cites doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3: Demonstrates claims 1 and 2 for an indirect comparison specifically, varying eligibility criteria that define both the network and the target population..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
:   **open / overstated.** Evidence-set selection can materially change network connectivity, available contrasts, precision, and conclusions, so C1 and the underlying robustness problem are valid. C2 conflates the population represented by the selected studies with the externally defined target population; study selection changes evidential relevance to a target but should not itself define the target estimand. Target-trial principles can help prespecify eligibility and estimand attributes, but calling evidence-set assembly target-trial emulation does not recover excluded information or identify selection effects. C4 is a reasonable sensitivity strategy if defensible networks are specified by transparent rules, although an undefined multiverse of all defensible networks invites further researcher discretion and multiplicity. The assertions that every inclusion decision is outcome-aware and that alternatives are usually or never reported are unsupported universal claims. This can be critical when eligibility was selected after results were known, but it is not automatically a modeling failure in every ITC.

Grok 4.5, recency lens
:   **partially-solved / supported-with-caveat.** The claim that eligibility and comparator choices can favor a network or target population before modeling, and that only one defensible network is typically shown, remains faithful for HTA/ITC practice. Recent work does, however, implement the multiverse response for treatment/network assembly in evidence synthesis, so the problem is not open as if no method existed. Vinatier et al. (2024) ran a multiverse covering all possible NMAs on different treatment combinations in antidepressants and showed large vibration of effects, especially for indirect comparisons. Guelimi et al. (2025) quantified how inclusion criteria and other methodological choices change NMA conclusions in psoriasis and explicitly contrasted their design with prior all-possible-networks work. These papers substantiate C1/C4 as live, demonstrated issues and give a usable multiverse template. They do not solve sponsor-side selective assembly, protocol-first eligibility fixed before knowing results, or target-trial emulation applied to the evidence set itself (C3); those remain open. RoB-NMA (2025) and PRISMA-NMA update work improve transparency of synthesis bias but do not replace multiverse reporting of defensible networks.
    Cites doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848: Demonstrates multiverse/all-possible-NMA analysis over treatment selection and shows large vibration of effects; partially resolves the proposed multiverse response to selective network assembly (C4) for treatment inclusion..
    Cites doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02558-6: Shows inclusion criteria and methodological choices alter NMA conclusions; supports that assembly decisions matter before modeling (C1) and that sensitivity over alternative networks is operational..
